topIssues.title: [PCD Milestone 4] Artifacts persistence over workflow phases
topIssues.author: 0xiamflux
topIssues.body:
## Context
On the permissionless codepath the deployment runs in two phases around the prestate. The first phase calculates everything that can be computed off-chain and persists the resulting artifacts. The run then pauses until the prestate, which produced out-of-band, is available to the workflow, it then proceeds to submit the deploy. If the prestate never arrives, the workflow must report a timeout failure rather than wait for ever.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] On the permissionless path, the first phase derives the off-chain artifacts and persists them.
- [ ] The run pauses after the first phase and waits for the produced prestate before continuing.
- [ ] The wait timeouts if the prestate never arrives; the run fails and alerts instead of hanging.
- [ ] Tests cover the first-phase persist of the artifacts, the timeout path, and resume.

topIssues.title: [PCD Milestone 4] Netchef workflow for Creating Netwokrs
topIssues.author: 0xiamflux
topIssues.body:
## Context

Today `netchef`'s workflows drive the whole L1 deployment through a single `op-deployer apply` invocation. It must support both permissioned and permissionless deployments, chosen from the network's listed features in the manifest. A permissionless deployment requires an `op-deployer` version new enough to run the PCD flow. When the manifest requests permissionless games but the pinned `op-deployer` is too old, `netchef` must fail during validation, with a clear message. Permissioned deployments continue on the existing apply codepath across all `op-deployer` versions.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] netchef selects the deployment path from the manifest's permissioned/permissionless feature.
- [ ] A permissionless deployment against an `op-deployer` or OPCM release that cannot support it fails during validation.
- [ ] Permissioned deployments are unchanged, using the same path and artifacts as today, on all supported `op-deployer` versions.
- [ ] Test suite covers path selection and each failure case.
- [ ] Regression tests for permissioned deployments pass.

topPRs.title: feat(rust): karst-derive inlined derivation pipeline
topPRs.author: theochap
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Adds `kona-karst-derive`, a flat, inlined OP Stack derivation pipeline that replaces the staged `kona-derive` architecture
- Single `Pipeline` struct holds all intermediate state as fields; all derivation steps are direct method calls (no trait-based stage composition)
- Only supports **Holocene+**, removing all hardfork branching: always uses channel assembler, batch validator, Fjord size limits, and Holocene frame pruning
- Re-exports traits and error types from `kona-derive` for compatibility

### Key simplifications vs kona-derive

| kona-derive | karst-derive |
|---|---|
| `ChannelProvider` mux (bank vs assembler) | Always assembler (inline) |
| `BatchProvider` mux (queue vs validator) | Always validator (inline) |
| `BatchStream.is_active()` guard | Always active |
| `FrameQueue` conditional Holocene pruning | Always prune |
| Fjord vs Bedrock `MAX_RLP_BYTES_PER_CHANNEL` | Always Fjord (`100_000_000`) |
| Recursive signal-based reset | Single flat `reset()` method |

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p kona-karst-derive` compiles
- [x] `cargo clippy -p kona-karst-derive` passes with zero warnings
- [ ] Port key unit tests from kona-derive stages
- [ ] Integration testing with rollup node

topPRs.title: Feat/kona pluggable dap and handler
topPRs.author: tonyvelichko
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds two narrow extension points to the kona rollup node so downstream OP Stack variants can plug in a custom `DataAvailabilityProvider` and/or a custom gossip `Handler` without forking the node service. Both extension points are introduced via default-bound generics, so every existing call site compiles unchanged and the default path is behaviourally identical to upstream.

Three commits, all under `rust/kona/`:

  - `feat(kona/gossip): generic Handler injection seam` — `GossipDriver`, `NetworkDriver`, `NetworkActor`, and their builders become generic over `H: Handler` (default `BlockHandler`). Adds `build_with_handler` / `with_handler` constructors. The `Handler` trait grows `l2_chain_id() / topic() / encode()` so the driver can dispatch generically; `BlockHandler` implements them by delegating to its inherent methods.
  - `feat(kona/providers-alloy): generic OnlinePipeline<DAP>` — `OnlinePipeline` gains a `DAP` type parameter (default `OnlineDataProvider`). Adds `new_polled_with_dap` / `new_indexed_with_dap` constructors that mirror `new_polled` / `new_indexed` shape-for-shape, taking a caller-supplied `DataAvailabilityProvider`.
  - `feat(kona/service): generic RollupNode<DAP, H>` — `RollupNode` and `RollupNodeBuilder` become generic over `(DAP, H)` with the same defaults. Adds `RollupNodeBuilder::with_data_availability_provider(factory)` and `with_block_handler(handler, signer_tx)`, both of which flip the corresponding type parameter. Factory closures run inside `RollupNode::start` so overrides receive the kona-built L1 chain provider and blob provider.

  No public API is removed or renamed. The default-types builder keeps the no-arg `build()`; only the custom-types path uses `build_with_overrides()`.

  **Tests**

  Three new unit tests cover the override seams:

  - `test_handler_trait_shims_match_inherent_methods` (`crates/node/gossip/src/handler.rs`) — calls `Handler::topic / l2_chain_id / topics` through `&dyn Handler` to verify the trait dispatch reaches the inherent `BlockHandler` methods.
  - `test_default_handler_matches_build_handler` (`crates/node/service/src/actors/network/builder.rs`) — asserts `NetworkBuilder::default_handler()` produces the same chain-id and rollup-config wiring the default `build()` path used.
  - `test_build_with_handler_installs_caller_handler` — exercises `NetworkBuilder::build_with_handler` with a stub `Handler` impl and confirms the custom handler is installed on the resulting `GossipDriver`.

 The default path preserves bit-identical construction order, so the entire existing test suite covers it.

  **Additional context**

  The motivation is to remove the ongoing maintenance tax for downstream OP Stack variants that today have no choice but to fork `RollupNode::start`, `OnlinePipeline`, and `NetworkActor` to substitute a DA source or a gossip validation rule. Every kona release bump becomes a manual three-way merge for those downstream forks.

  The seams are the minimum needed to unblock that use case:

  - The `DataAvailabilityProvider` and `Handler` traits already exist publicly in kona — the patches just let them actually be used as extension points, which is presumably why they exist as traits.
  - All extension points use default-bound generics rather than `Box<dyn Trait>`, so the default path has zero runtime cost and the override path keeps full type information (the pipeline stage chain needs the DAP's associated `Item` type at compile time).
  - Factory closures (rather than pre-built instances) let kona finish constructing its own L1 chain / blob providers before calling the override, so the consumer doesn't have to reconstruct them.

  Concrete consumer: a downstream rollup variant that filters L1 batcher transactions by a set membership rule, which requires both a custom DA source (filter at the L1 layer) and a custom gossip validation rule (rotating valid-set per epoch). With these seams, that variant can stay a thin set of crates depending on kona instead of a hard fork.
